situations.name: Credential entry form
situations.definition: Render a connector's declared field schema as a validated form that captures API keys/secrets and saves an encrypted credential.
situations.note: CredentialEditForm is the real owner, but four parallel shells wrap it (schema form, template form, negotiator field-capture, autoCred review) each re-deciding validation, naming, and save/rollback semantics.

situations.name: Secret value handling in UI
situations.definition: Hold a plaintext secret in the renderer long enough to save it without leaking it into React state, DevTools, Sentry, or the persisted blob.
situations.note: The ref-not-state discipline is documented in comments in three separate files rather than encoded in one primitive, so each new secret-bearing surface has to rediscover it.

situations.name: Secret reveal control
situations.definition: Mask a stored/entered secret in the UI with an explicit reveal, copy, and paste affordance.
situations.note: Each site re-derives isSecret from inputType === 'password' and re-implements the eye toggle; there is no SecretInput primitive, so masking policy is a per-file decision.

situations.name: OAuth connect flow
situations.definition: Kick off a provider consent handshake, poll for completion, and land a token reference on the credential without token material crossing IPC.
situations.note: Genuinely converged on useOAuthProtocol; the remaining hazard is the session-ref redemption contract (client never sees the refresh token) which lives only in comments.

situations.name: Just-in-time auth prompt
situations.definition: Surface a mid-call authorization-required error as a consent URL the user can open, then retry the original operation.
situations.note: Low recurrence, high consequence: every command that can hit an MCP gateway must remember to narrow AppError.kind === 'authorization_required' or the user just sees a raw error.

situations.name: Connection healthcheck
situations.definition: Run a live probe against a credential or a connection config and show pass/fail/unverifiable with a durable result.
situations.note: The three-layer result contract (module cache > persisted metadata > store pass-through) and the third 'unverifiable' state are subtle enough that plugin-side connection tests (obsidian, gitlab) ignore them entirely and hand-roll booleans.

situations.name: Connection health indicator
situations.definition: Render one compact dot/badge that answers 'is this connection working right now' from several independent signals.
situations.note: Shared StatusDot/StatusBadge/ConnectionStatusBadge all exist and vault uses none of them; CompositeHealthDot even hand-rolls a title= tooltip. Fleet solved the same problem well in isolation (FleetStatusDots) with no cross-pollination.

situations.name: Connector catalog browse
situations.definition: Present the full connector catalog as a filterable, searchable grid so the user can pick what to connect.
situations.note: Five filter axes (connected/purpose/category/license/role) live in usePickerFilters, but embedded pickers used from templates and build flows re-filter the vault with their own ad-hoc service_type matching.

situations.name: Connector gating in a feature
situations.definition: Decide whether a feature is usable by checking the user's vault for a specific connector, and prompt them to connect it if not.
situations.note: Fifteen plugin files call useVaultStore and each re-derives connected/healthy with its own credentials.find(c => c.service_type === X); there is no useCredentialFor(serviceType) selector, so 'is this feature usable' is answered fifteen slightly different ways.

situations.name: Deep-link into vault
situations.definition: Navigate the user from an unrelated feature to a specific vault sub-view (catalog, add-new, databases) to unblock a task.
situations.note: Three transports coexist for the same intent — the nav context, a storeBus event for callers outside the provider tree, and setSidebarSection + navigate pairs sprinkled in features; a pendingKey buffer papers over the mount-order race.

situations.name: Multi-phase flow machine
situations.definition: Model a multi-step credential/plugin flow (consent to work to review to done, with error and cancel) as explicit states rather than a pile of booleans.
situations.note: The repo has both a validated FSM lib and a useWizardReducer, and exactly one file in this slice uses the former while ~22 hand-roll string unions; illegal transitions and reset-completeness are re-litigated per flow.

situations.name: Wizard with gated steps
situations.definition: Walk a user through a fixed ordered sequence of setup steps with per-step validation and a progress rail.
situations.note: Every wizard reinvents its own step indicator geometry and its own next-gating rule; PipelineRail is the only one built to serve two modes and it lives inside one plugin.

situations.name: Informed-consent gate
situations.definition: Name exactly what a privileged local action will read or do, and require an explicit user click before it runs.
situations.note: ForagingConsent's own docstring says it 'mirrors AutoCredConsent's structure' — the pattern is acknowledged as shared but was copied, so a new privileged action can ship with a weaker disclosure and nothing catches it.

situations.name: Approve/reject decision surface
situations.definition: Show a proposed action or AI draft with approve, reject, and reason controls that commit a real side effect.
situations.note: A shared DecisionRow/DecisionActions primitive exists but only overview consumes it; vault, companion, twin and fleet each hand-roll busy state, button pairs, and reject-reason presets (two files literally duplicate the same REJECT_PRESETS array).

situations.name: Destructive action confirm
situations.definition: Block an irreversible operation behind a confirm that states what will break, and keep it bound to the context it was raised in.
situations.note: Two unrelated answers coexist — a modal confirm and an inline arm-then-click-again state machine copied three times — and the genuinely hard part (context drift: useQuerySafeMode pins the runQuery closure, FleetProcessScanner re-resolves the PID because the confirm can outlive its target) is encoded in neither.

situations.name: Mutating-query safe mode
situations.definition: Detect that a user-authored SQL statement mutates data and require a second confirmation before executing it.
situations.note: Correctness rests on isMutationQuery's tokenizer keeping up with dialects; a false negative silently runs a DELETE against a user's production database.

situations.name: SQL editor and result grid
situations.definition: Give the user a syntax-highlighted query editor plus a paged, typed result table against a live external database.
situations.note: The textarea-over-highlighted-pre technique means scroll sync, tab handling, and IME behavior are all bespoke; it works but nothing else in the app can reuse it for a non-SQL language.

situations.name: Remote resource scope picker
situations.definition: After connecting, let the user narrow a credential to specific remote resources fetched live from the provider, including dependent chains.
situations.note: Least-privilege scoping done once, correctly (topo-sorted depends_on, stale-pick detection, skip-saves-{} vs never-prompted-null) — but it is one file with no test coverage of the dependency-invalidation path.

situations.name: App-root modal host
situations.definition: Show a modal that must outlive the subtree that requested it, and let the caller await its outcome.
situations.note: A promise-returning module store plus one host at App root — the right answer, solved for exactly one modal; every other flow that unmounts mid-modal (catalog form after save, autoCred reset) has to know to route through it.

situations.name: Nested modal stacking
situations.definition: Open a secondary dialog on top of an existing modal without the Escape key or backdrop click closing both.
situations.note: Child modals opt out of BaseModal and hand-roll fixed inset-0 backdrops plus a capture-phase Escape stopPropagation, precisely because BaseModal has no stacking/z-order contract.

situations.name: Local file and folder picker
situations.definition: Let the user choose a directory or files on disk and show the chosen path back to them.
situations.note: Some call a backend command (kbPickDirectory), most import @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog directly; default directory, filter list, path display, empty state, and error handling are re-decided at every call site and none validate the returned path before use.

situations.name: File drop-zone ingestion
situations.definition: Accept files dragged onto a region and hand their paths to a backend ingestion or upload command.
situations.note: Only the glow is shared; the load-bearing part — that Tauri exposes a non-standard file.path and the drop silently no-ops when it is missing — is re-derived per drop zone.

situations.name: Vector KB ingestion
situations.definition: Load documents (files, directory scan, pasted text) into a per-credential vector knowledge base and track chunking progress.
situations.note: Four entry points (drop, directory, text, drive bridge) each return a jobId and wire their own progress listener; kb_id lives inside a JSON metadata blob parsed inline, and Drive feature-detects the whole KB lane by probing for an unregistered command.

situations.name: Background job progress
situations.definition: Show that a backend-owned multi-minute job is running, survive unmount or reload, and reconcile with terminal events.
situations.note: The single most-repeated situation in the slice: companion converged internally on a jobsById model and every other plugin plus vault rebuilt rehydrate-from-backend, re-attach-on-mount, cancel, and terminal-event reconciliation from scratch — eight distinct job-lifecycle designs, no useBackgroundJob hook, despite a shared src-tauri/src/background_job.rs underneath.

situations.name: Live-refresh polling loop
situations.definition: Keep a panel's data fresh on an interval without stacking timers, hammering the backend, or running while the window is hidden.
situations.note: The worst divergence in the slice: a real usePolling with a coordinator, error backoff, a named cadence registry and tab-visibility pause exists, and exactly ONE of ~21 polling sites here (GitLab) uses it — the other 20 hand-roll setInterval and poll a hidden window forever.

situations.name: Plugin panel shell
situations.definition: Frame a plugin's sub-surfaces in the shared content shell and switch between its tabs.
situations.note: The shell is shared but tab state is not: artist/obsidian/research-lab persist the active tab in systemStore and lazy-load each panel, GitLab keeps it in local state and imports eagerly — so deep-link, tour restore, and code-splitting differ per plugin.

situations.name: Plugin enable gating
situations.definition: Turn a whole plugin on or off from a catalog and reflect that in the sidebar and nav.
situations.note: One hand-rolled toggle over an enabledPlugins Set rather than the shared AccessibleToggle; fine at n=1 but it is the only place that defines what 'a plugin' is to the shell.

situations.name: Plugin connection setup panel
situations.definition: Build the gating first-tab of a plugin where the user establishes and tests a connection to the external system it wraps.
situations.note: Three structurally different connect flows (token lookup + instance URL, folder browse + test-then-save, OAuth button) with visually similar chrome and no shared shell; SetupPanel's comment records a real leak where a successful test flipped global connected state before Save.

situations.name: External vault sync and conflict
situations.definition: Push and pull data between the app and an external store, surfacing per-item conflicts for manual resolution.
situations.note: Local vault sync has full LCS line-diff conflict resolution; cloud sync is bidirectional over the same content with no conflict concept at all — a silent last-writer-wins data-loss path.

situations.name: Composition autosave
situations.definition: Debounce-persist an in-progress editable document to an autosave slot while also supporting explicit save, save-as, open, and a recents list.
situations.note: The only real data-loss protection in the slice, built once: debounced autosave, explicit save clears the autosave, restore hint on reopen. Research Lab's editable forms and vault's design drafts have nothing equivalent.

situations.name: Document signing and verification
situations.definition: Cryptographically sign a file, write or import a sidecar signature, and verify a file against it.
situations.note: Clean single-hook ownership; the fragile part is absolute-to-drive-relative path translation kept consistent across sign, verify, and history — get it wrong and a valid signature reads as tampered.

situations.name: OCR extraction surface
situations.definition: Extract text from an image or PDF through a selectable backend, then preview, copy, or save the result.
situations.note: Backend choice (hosted vision vs local CLI) carries asymmetric cancel semantics — one has an operation_id abort, the other cannot be cancelled at all — encoded nowhere but this hook.

situations.name: Direct external API client
situations.definition: Call a third-party HTTP API straight from the renderer with a timeout, a caller abort signal, and typed errors.
situations.note: Two structurally twin clients independently arrived at the same timeout-plus-AbortSignal-plus-kind-tagged-error convention; nothing extracts it, and unlike vault's api-proxy path these bypass the backend entirely.

situations.name: Media lightbox viewer
situations.definition: Preview an image, video, or PDF full-screen with zoom, pan, rotate, and keyboard navigation across a set.
situations.note: Near-identical zoom-clamp, drag-pan, wheel-zoom and arrow-key mechanics written twice with different zoom ranges and feature sets.

situations.name: Playback transport engine
situations.definition: Drive a play/pause/seek transport whose clock ticks many times a second without putting the time in React state.
situations.note: Both reached the same ref-plus-subscriber shape, but one bridges two real media engines with watchdogs and crossfade while the other is a pure rAF clock — no shared transport abstraction to inherit.

situations.name: Run history log
situations.definition: List past runs of a repeatable operation with status and a way to inspect or replay one.
situations.note: Three are DB-backed and survive restart while creative-session history lives only in a Zustand slice — same surface, different durability tier, undocumented.

situations.name: Drag-to-move and reorder
situations.definition: Drag items within a list or tree to move them into a container or reorder them via a custom dataTransfer payload.
situations.note: Drive converged on one moveManyInto only after a documented bug where one of four drop targets had drifted without the move-into-own-ancestor guard; artist reinvented its own MIME vocabulary with no shared drag primitive.

situations.name: State-change desktop notification
situations.definition: Detect a backend entity crossing into a terminal state and raise an OS notification plus an in-app entry.
situations.note: One implementation covers permission request, active-to-terminal transition detection and per-user prefs; every other long job in the slice (revitalize, ingestion, autoCred) finishes silently.

situations.name: Design variant tab switcher
situations.definition: Scaffold several visual variants of a surface behind a small tab strip during active design iteration.
situations.note: Explicitly throwaway scaffolding with a documented removal condition — the risk is that nothing enforces the removal, so variants ship.

situations.name: Tauri event subscription
situations.definition: Subscribe a component to a backend-emitted event stream and unsubscribe cleanly across StrictMode double-mounts.
situations.note: A shared useTauriEvent exists with ~20 users while 23 files still import listen directly; the async-unlisten race that leaks a subscription on fast unmount is re-solved (or missed) per file.

situations.name: Module-scope warm cache
situations.definition: Keep fetched data alive at module scope so several components share one request and a fully-unmounted route repaints warm instead of re-ghosting.
situations.note: Vault uses the shared createModuleCache with refcounted loading and an unmounted guard; the plugins each hand-roll a module Map with a different eviction policy (byte-budget LRU, entry-count LRU, refcount-release, bare boolean) for the same doctrine in docs/design/overview-loading.md.

situations.name: Browser-automation harvest
situations.definition: Drive a real browser session on the user's behalf to walk a provider's console and extract a credential, with a live action log and cancel.
situations.note: The highest-authority flow in the slice: it types into a real provider console and writes what it scrapes into the encrypted vault. Transport-only keys are stripped by a __ prefix convention that only exists inside one save() body.

situations.name: Local secret discovery
situations.definition: Scan the machine or a pasted blob for existing secrets, classify them to services, and let the user select which to import.
situations.note: Foraging (reads .env/.aws/.kube/.ssh from disk) and Import (parses pasted blobs) solve the same select-and-map-then-create problem with two unrelated state machines and two selection models.

situations.name: Local app and MCP discovery
situations.definition: Detect installed desktop apps or MCP servers on the machine and register them as connectors after a capability review.
situations.note: Approving a manifest grants capabilities with per-capability risk levels; the risk vocabulary lives in an API constants map rather than anywhere the design system can enforce.

situations.name: AI-assisted connector authoring
situations.definition: Turn a plain-language request into a working connector definition (fields, healthcheck, setup docs) and iterate on it with the user.
situations.note: Design, negotiator, and autoCred are three LLM-driven paths to the same artifact with three phase machines and three refinement idioms; only the design path has a refinement counter.

situations.name: AI draft with human edit
situations.definition: Generate text or a set of candidate rows as the AI, land them in an editable draft, and require an explicit save before anything commits.
situations.note: Companion's two chat cards converged on a durable resolveChatCard contract; seven other surfaces rebuild the drafting-spinner + regenerate + steer-input trio independently, and one (ReportPreviewDrawer) skips the review step entirely and writes AI output straight to storage.

situations.name: Guided setup instructions
situations.definition: Render provider setup docs as an interactive, resumable checklist with clickable links and persisted step completion.
situations.note: Step identity is a hash of the markdown, so any doc edit silently orphans the user's saved progress; the reset-then-restore ordering is a comment-documented landmine.

situations.name: External URL opening
situations.definition: Send the user to a provider or docs URL in their real browser from inside the desktop app.
situations.note: Vault always routes model/provider-supplied URLs through sanitizeExternalUrl; plugins (radio, artist, dev-tools, fleet) and even PendingAuthModal open raw strings, some of them backend- or LLM-derived.

situations.name: Third-party API playground
situations.definition: Let the user browse a connector's endpoints, build a request with real auth, fire it, and read the response.
situations.note: Requests go through a backend proxy so the secret is never in the renderer, but responses are rendered verbatim — a provider echoing a token back lands it in the DOM with no redaction pass.

situations.name: API spec import
situations.definition: Accept an OpenAPI/Postman spec by file, paste, or catalog and merge its endpoints into an existing endpoint list.
situations.note: mergeEndpoints has to reconcile three sources (saved, catalog, user-supplied) with no stable endpoint identity beyond method+path.

situations.name: MCP tool invocation surface
situations.definition: List a gateway's tools, build typed inputs for one, invoke it, and render a structured result.
situations.note: Vault's playground invokes tools directly while companion's panel blocks a fleet session on human approval of the same call; the two surfaces share the tool vocabulary but neither the approval nor the auth-required handling.

situations.name: Credential rotation policy
situations.definition: Configure a rotation schedule for a credential, show the countdown, and expose rotate-now plus rotation history.
situations.note: Rotating an in-use credential can break every persona bound to it; the blast radius lives in a different sub-feature (sub_dependencies) than the rotate button.

situations.name: Entity audit trail view
situations.definition: Show the append-only operation history for one entity with filtering and paging.
situations.note: AuditLogTable hardcodes English operation labels in an OP_LABELS map (an i18n hole) and re-implements paging; the broker's activity trail solves the same shape again with an expand/collapse instead.

situations.name: Credential kill-switch
situations.definition: List every external consumer that has used a credential through the audited proxy and let the operator revoke one immediately.
situations.note: A single-file security surface whose whole value is that secrets never appear in it; the honest exclusion note (what the broker does NOT cover) is prose in one panel, not an invariant anything enforces.

situations.name: Entity relationship graph
situations.definition: Draw an interactive node graph of how entities relate, with layout, selection, filtering, and (in vault) revocation simulation.
situations.note: Three answers to one question: vault hand-rolls canvas plus its own layout and hit-testing, research-lab uses @xyflow/react, and obsidian's 'Graph' tab is not a graph at all but a stats dashboard — so grepping for the graph implementation finds three incompatible things. Vault's also fans out one dependents call per credential on mount.

situations.name: Per-entity event subscription
situations.definition: Let the user turn platform events on or off for one entity and configure each event's parameters inline.
situations.note: Connector-declared events and universal rotation templates are merged client-side by id, and in-flight toggles are deduped with two separate ref Sets — rules that only exist inside this one component.

situations.name: Backend token to remediation
situations.definition: Turn a language-agnostic backend status token into a localized label plus a concrete 'here is how to fix it' line.
situations.note: tokenLabel is the sanctioned path but AuditLogTable and several error configs still ship English label maps; the backend also sends a pre-built English detail string that can never be localized, so the UI has to ignore it.

situations.name: Live PTY terminal viewer
situations.definition: Attach a durable streaming terminal to a running CLI process so scrollback survives unmount and remount.
situations.note: Instances are keyed by sessionId and attach/detach rather than dispose, specifically to survive StrictMode double-invoke; a naive per-mount xterm silently drops a live agent's output.

situations.name: Log tail viewer
situations.definition: Show an auto-scrolling, capped line buffer of a background process's stdout that is not an interactive terminal.
situations.note: Each site re-implements scroll-to-bottom, tail capping, and (in autoCred) near-duplicate line collapsing; no LogTail primitive despite an identical shape four times.

situations.name: Findings triage queue
situations.definition: Route an auto-raised finding to an autonomous runner or an interactive session, with provenance and later verification.
situations.note: Converged because it got a design doc; dispatch can autonomously open PRs and spend LLM budget, gated only by an unattended_mode flag.

situations.name: Entity switcher dropdown
situations.definition: Let the user search and switch among parallel entities of one kind (projects, conversations, twins) from a compact control.
situations.note: Three different widgets over the same DevProject list inside one plugin, plus two more elsewhere ranging from a plain dropdown to a full keyboard-navigable command menu.

situations.name: Bulk multi-select dispatch
situations.definition: Let the user check a subset of items in a list or grid and fire one action across all of them, tolerating partial failure.
situations.note: Eleven hand-rolled Set<string> toggle/selectAll/clear implementations with a per-item try/catch loop and a three-way success/partial/fail report; only one was extracted into a hook and even that is not reused by its own sibling plugin.

situations.name: Diff and patch preview
situations.definition: Show a human exactly what changed between two versions of text or config before they commit to an action.
situations.note: Two independent diff algorithms (a hand-rolled line LCS and a counts-only delta summary) plus a third preview shape for imported secrets; no shared DiffView.

situations.name: Coverage matrix grid
situations.definition: Render an NxM crosstab where cell intensity communicates coverage and clicking a cell dispatches an action.
situations.note: Three bespoke CSS-grid crosstabs with independent hover, tooltip, and color-scale logic; explicitly not a data table, so the table primitive does not help.

situations.name: Skill catalog and apply
situations.definition: Let a user search a library of reusable skills and either apply one to a live session or install it into a repo.
situations.note: Fleet and dev-tools each own a full parallel stack (data hook, list UI, confirm modal) for pick-a-skill-and-do-something-with-it.

situations.name: OS process reconciliation
situations.definition: Find processes the in-memory registry lost track of and let the user resume or kill them safely.
situations.note: PIDs are OS-recycled, so the kill path re-resolves against a live scan first; a stale-PID kill would terminate an unrelated process on the user's machine.

situations.name: Token and cost rollup
situations.definition: Aggregate LLM token, cache, and spend numbers into a glanceable summary at session and fleet granularity.
situations.note: Money-adjacent and split across two unrelated data paths: fleet reads its own transcript rollup, dev-tools goes through multi-provider tracing adapters; the two can disagree about the same spend.

situations.name: Policy threshold settings card
situations.definition: Offer a small persisted settings card (toggle plus numeric bound) that pushes an operator policy live to the backend.
situations.note: The identical card shell is hand-typed four times in one folder; copy-paste convergence, which drifts the moment one of them gets a new affordance.

situations.name: Streaming chat transcript
situations.definition: Render a live, paginated message list that swaps a streaming placeholder for the persisted turn when it lands.
situations.note: Companion's is careful (keyset cursors, focus-read-at-event-time); the vault database ChatTab solves the same 'assistant conversation over a data source' job with a naive setInterval poll and no pagination.

situations.name: Idempotent send guard
situations.definition: Guarantee a user-initiated dispatch happens exactly once, even across double-clicks, retries, or an app restart.
situations.note: Companion has a durable localStorage nonce ledger; vault's equivalents are bare in-flight ref Sets that reset on reload, so a mid-save refresh can double-create.

situations.name: Voice input and playback
situations.definition: Capture speech to text through the user's chosen engine and speak responses back with volume and level control.
situations.note: Playback converged, capture did not: the composer mic bypasses the engine-aware hook and always uses cloud STT even when the user selected on-device whisper — a silent privacy regression.

situations.name: Local model install
situations.definition: Download and install an on-device model or sidecar binary with a progress bar, cancel, and failure state.
situations.note: The shared install block covers engine binaries; the per-model download list re-implements the same percent/failed bar rather than extending it.

situations.name: Readiness completion score
situations.definition: Derive a 0-100 'how set up is this' score from independent milestones and let the user jump to the weakest gap.
situations.note: Badge, popover, and checklist all read one Gap shape so score and triage list cannot disagree — the model to copy for the vault's own setup-readiness surfaces, which have no equivalent.

situations.name: Grounding preview
situations.definition: Show the user which memories or documents the AI actually retrieved before answering.
situations.note: Three unrelated shapes for 'here is what I retrieved and how relevant it was' — an event-driven strip, an on-demand panel, and a KB search result list — with three different score/snippet renderings.

situations.name: Tier-gated UI
situations.definition: Hide or simplify a surface based on the user's product tier without leaving a broken hole in the layout.
situations.note: Converged on useTier, but each call site invents its own simplification (hide column, hide button, hide whole modal) with no shared gating component.

situations.name: Data table
situations.definition: Render tabular data with loading, empty, and row-entrance states.
situations.note: Documented elsewhere. In this slice 10 raw <table> implementations vs 3 UnifiedTable consumers.

situations.name: Modal dialog
situations.definition: Open a focus-trapped overlay panel over the current surface.
situations.note: Documented elsewhere. BaseModal is used pervasively in dev-tools/fleet, but 19 files across the slice still hand-roll a fixed inset-0 backdrop, mostly for nested or drawer-shaped overlays.

situations.name: Page and section loading
situations.definition: Cover a lazy route or async data region while it warms without flashing an empty state.
situations.note: Documented elsewhere. 8 RouteChunkSkeleton users; vault modals still fall back to a centered spinner, and shape-matched skeletons are hand-built per section.
